messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: hosted-runtime OOM spike on kv-cache nodes (mem pressure) — alert group=kv-cache, severity=high, signal=kv_mem_usage > 95% for 3m
oncall_emily: Acknowledged. Joining bridge now. Anyone see an obvious customer?
sre_mike: seeing sustained growth in per-session KV size, looks like prefixes keep accumulating. p95 kv map per-session ~1.8GB, nodes hitting OOM kill-snap.
runtime_lee: logs show many sessions with identical early-system messages appended repeatedly — likely a client loop. Example: "system: you are assistant" repeated inside user messages.
eng_karen: oh that matches a recent SDK change to persist chat_history into system prompt on reconnects. Rolling that out yesterday to hosted customers.
support_ana: I can query affected orgs quickly. Running search for sessions with >500k tokens in prefix.
product_jess: customer-facing impact? latency? Are any customer requests failing 5xx?
sre_mike: yes, increased 5xx from runtime as OOMs happen. Some requests are timing out while node restarts. We have ~12% of hosts cycling in the last 30m.
oncall_emily: Triage plan: 1) short-term mitigation to prevent immediate OOMs 2) identify impacted customers and throttle 3) rollback/patch SDK change 4) postmortem.
runtime_lee: Quick mitigation options: disable prefetch KV population for hosted pool, force aggressive evictions, and reduce continuous batching max_batch_window to 50ms.
eng_karen: Can we flip a runtime flag centrally? I can push a config to the hosted control plane. Suggested flags:
```
kvcache.prefetch.enabled=false
kvcache.max_per_session_bytes=536870912  # 512MB
batching.max_window_ms=50
```
eng_karen: pushing to canary now for 10% of traffic.
sre_mike: monitoring — canary nodes dropped mem usage ~40% within 2 min. No immediate errors on canary.
oncall_emily: Good. Roll to 100% with safety checks, but do it in waves. Coordinate with support for customer notices.
eng_karen: Rolling 25% -> 50% -> 100% over 10min. Executing: `./controlplane rollout --flag kvcache.prefetch.enabled=false --wave 25`
support_ana: Listing impacted orgs now, will DM oncall with org ids. Found 3 high-volume customers with repeated reconnects.
product_jess: Notify account teams for those 3. Might be closing user sessions will help too.
sre_mike: After 100% rollout, mem pressure decreased cluster-wide. OOM occurrences dropped to 0 in last 5m. 5xx rate returning toward baseline.
oncall_emily: Great. Next: rollback the SDK change for reconnect persistence and prepare a durable fix (hard cap on per-session kv and sanitize system insertion).
eng_karen: Agree. Creating hotfix PR to change reconnect behavior + add server-side guard for `kvcache.max_per_session_bytes`.
runtime_lee: Also scheduling a patch to make the eviction policy LRU with hysteresis to avoid simultaneous mass-evictions causing perf cliffs.
sre_mike: Metrics to capture for postmortem: per-session kv distribution, batch window sizes, rollout timestamps, affected host list, customer request ids.
support_ana: I've opened ticket INF-4821 for each affected org and added temporary mitigation steps for customers (restart sessions, reduce reconnect frequency).
product_jess: We'll prepare a customer-facing note for the 3 orgs. No widespread outage but degraded for some.
oncall_emily: Handoff: I'm briefing night oncall. @sre_mike and @runtime_lee stay on standby for 30m. Confirming next oncall: @eng_karen will be primary for the SDK rollback tomorrow morning.
eng_karen: noted. I'll include test to simulate maliciously long prefix to prevent regressions.
sre_mike: Adding temporary alert: fire when average per-session kv > 400MB for 5m.
oncall_emily: Thanks everyone. Create postmortem ticket and include timeline + customer impact. I'll update incident status in #incidents. :white_check_mark:
